Welcome to the Reproducible Analytical Pipelines (RAP) Accelerator. A programme for ICB analysts starting their RAP journey, building the foundational skills to apply these approaches in practice. This programme runs from October – December 2026 and is funded by the Strategic Commissioning Intelligence Centre (SCIC).

title: Prerequisites & expectations
text:
💬 During the sessions
As the RAP Accelerator is run in a flipped classroom style, the sessions are highly engaging — don’t expect to just sit back and watch! To get the most out of the programme, here’s what we ask of you:

Complete the pre-work: 60–90 minutes before each session. Essential, not optional.
Camera on: we’ll work in small groups, and we learn best when we can see each other.
Engage actively: ask questions, work through examples, share what you’re learning.
Bring a real project: the capstone project applies what you’ve learnt to something that matters to you.

title: Prerequisites & expectations
text:
🧑‍🏫 Need a quick refresher?
If you want to take part in the RAP accelerator but don’t yet meet the prerequisites, there is a chance for you to upskill before October.
The NHS Open Analytics community is running an Introduction to R and RStudio course in September. Attending this will ensure you meet the prerequisites. You can sign up online. On the sign-up form, please write that you heard about the workshop through SCIC.

title: About the programme
text:
RAP (Reproducible Analytical Pipelines) are a set of tools, principles, and techniques that enable analysts to create analytical processes that are automated, transparent, quality assured and reusable. This has the potential to increase efficiency and quality of analytical work across the healthcare system.
The Goldacre review recommended RAP as the minimum standard for academic and NHS data analysis.

title: About the programme
text:
🚀 What is the RAP Accelerator?
A programme for ICB analysts starting their RAP journey, building the foundational skills to apply these approaches in practice. Some coding experience is expected (see prerequisites), along with enthusiasm to learn.
It runs as a flipped classroom. You’ll work through learning material at your own pace before each session, then use session time with tutors for discussion, problem-solving, and going deeper.

Each session includes:

60 mins contact session with the tutors

We’ll also have an online community for attendees to ask questions to tutors or chat with peers running throughout the ten weeks.
We won’t cover:

Basic R or Python programming (We expect you to already know a little programming)
Plotting and visualisation
Modelling and machine learning
Using LLMs
Building interactive web apps

title: ♻️ Reusable
text:
Writing code that’s easy to understand and reuse, by others and by yourself months later is at the heart of RAP.
In this session, you’ll learn to write modular functions, document your functions, and follow consistent style conventions that make your work easy to read.

title: 🏆 Capstone
text:
🎯 Learning objectives
By the end of this session, you should be able to:

Apply RAP principles to an existing or new project
Conduct and receive peer feedback on your code
Plan and prioritise improvements to your analytical pipeline
Discuss trade-offs and make decisions about what to refactor and when

title: 🏆 Capstone
text:
💼 Your project

Bring your own
You’re welcome to bring an existing analytical project — anything from a one-off analysis to an ongoing pipeline. We’ll help you apply RAP principles incrementally.
What makes a good capstone project:

You care about it (it’s real work, or similar to real work you do)
It’s something you’ll actually use and maintain after the course
It’s complex enough to benefit from RAP (not a one-liner, but doesn’t need to be huge)



Use our example
If you don’t have a suitable project, we’ll provide an example analytical project that you can work through. You’ll learn the same principles but on our project instead of yours.

title: 🏆 Capstone
text:
📖 Before the session
For the capstone, there are no formal pre-learning materials. We’ll ask you to complete a short form, reflecting on your capstone project. We’ll ask you about:

What was the problem?
What RAP techniques did you apply?
How has that impacted your work?
What are you going to do next?

You can also use time before the session to work on your project. Remember you can always ask for help in the channel.

title: 🏆 Capstone
text:
🖥️ During the session
We’ll reflect on and share your projects, give feedback, and discuss next steps. This is as much about learning your own development process as it is about the code itself.

title: 👥 Collaborative
text:
In this session, you’ll learn the fundamentals of version control with Git and GitHub — the tools that let teams collaborate safely on code, track changes, and avoid losing work to a corrupted file or accidental overwrite.
You’ll also explore peer review and pair programming, and learn how to ask for help effectively when you get stuck.

title: Learner Personas
text: Some examples of the kinds of people that might come on the accelerator, and what they might learn

title: Learner Personas
text:
Riley Reports

Riley Reports has a lot of experience with performance reports and other forms of regular reporting across a number of NHS contexts
Over time they have developed advanced skills with Excel and Power Query to speed up reporting and add depth to analyses done with this data
They are now working in an ICB across a range of data with a lot of different types of questions across different datasets
They have learned a bit of R and have used it in anger a few times but they have heard about using R with RAP and want to know how it could help them
In particular Riley thinks that they could learn skills to allow other team members to pick up work while they’re off, have more robust and transparent processes for when things go awry, and maybe add a few statistical tools to the toolbox along the way

title: Learner Personas
text:
Patel Pipeline

Patel Pipeline has spent time in industry working on big datasets
They have a lot of experience working with SQL and Power Query formula language (M)
Before they started with the ICB their team was starting to use Python for data processing and they had started to learn more about using Python for data processing
At the moment they are the lead analyst in their area interested in moving data pipelines to Python and have had some early success
Patel Pipeline heard about RAP at an analyst huddle and thinks that ensuring data pipeline work is transparent, versioned, and robust will help them convince their team leader to encourage more of the team to move towards Python

title: Getting set up
text:
☁️ Cloud environment
If you have issues using R or Python on your work computer, we’ll set up a Binder as a backup. Binder is a free online environment where you can run code without installing anything. However, there are some limitations.

Changes aren’t saved between sessions
Takes time to load
Limited for later work on your own project

You’ll get much more from this programme if you’re able to work on your own machine.
